title: The Midnight Server Breach
subtitle: Valid credentials, an invalid person
briefing: NexaCore is a fortnight from a confidential product release. At 11:42 PM an internal monitor records a protected source archive being copied off a restricted development server. Nobody broke in. Valid employee credentials were used, a badge belonging to someone at home opened a side door, and a camera stopped recording for nineteen minutes.
solution: Ethan Blake's contractor account should have been revoked when his engagement ended. It was not. He borrowed Olivia's badge from the coat rack during his exit interview, entered through the side door, worked from Maya's unlocked workstation, and used Ryan's administrator credentials which he had watched being typed weeks earlier. The camera outage was Daniel's routine firmware push, and it simply happened to overlap.

topics.credentials: who could use the admin account
topics.badge: the badge used at the side door

suspects.name: Ryan Cole
suspects.relation: Owns the credentials that were used
suspects.motive: Full access to every system that was touched.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At home. My badge never touched the building after six, and you can check that.

statements.question: Your account did this. Explain that.
statements.text: Then somebody has my password. I have been saying so since the alert came in.

statements.question: Whose badge opened the side door?
statements.text: Not mine. Mine is in the log at 5:52 PM, going out.

suspects.name: Maya Chen
suspects.motive: Direct access to the development repositories.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: I left at quarter past eight. My partner will tell you when I got in.

statements.question: Your machine issued the commands.
statements.text: My machine was on. I do not lock it. That is a bad habit, not a crime.

statements.question: Whose badge opened the side door?
statements.text: I have no idea. Mine is on my keyring and my keyring was with me.

suspects.name: Daniel Ross
suspects.motive: Controls the building's cameras and door system.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: On the external patrol, as logged, every twenty minutes.

statements.question: Could you have used the admin account?
statements.text: I can open doors. I cannot open a repository. Ask anyone.

statements.question: Whose badge opened the side door?
statements.text: The system says Olivia Grant. I flagged it at the time and nobody called me back.

suspects.name: Olivia Grant
suspects.relation: Her badge was used at 11:31 PM
suspects.motive: Holds the confidential project documents that were taken.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At home from seven. My badge was in my coat pocket in the third floor cloakroom.

statements.question: Your badge opened the side door.
statements.text: Then somebody took it out of my coat. I noticed it missing the next morning.

statements.question: Could you have used the admin account?
statements.text: I cannot deploy a change without three approvals. I certainly cannot do this.

suspects.name: Ethan Blake
suspects.motive: His access was never revoked and his contract was terminated early.

statements.question: Where were you that night?
statements.text: At home. I do not even have a badge any more, so what would I be doing there?

statements.question: Could you have used the admin account?
statements.text: My account was disabled on Friday. Whatever this is, it is not me.

statements.question: Whose badge opened the side door?
statements.text: How would I know? I was let go. I am not on your systems.

statements.question: A USB device registered to you was connected.
statements.text: I returned all my equipment. If something has my name on it, someone else kept it.

evidence.name: Session history
evidence.description: Commands run from Maya's workstation at 11:36 PM by someone unfamiliar with the layout.

evidence.name: Archive access record
evidence.description: The protected archive was read at 11:42 PM under Ryan's administrator account.

evidence.name: Side door badge entry
evidence.description: Olivia Grant's badge opened the side door at 11:31 PM.

evidence.name: USB connection record
evidence.description: A USB mass storage device was connected at 11:44 PM.

evidence.name: Camera outage window
evidence.description: The server corridor camera recorded nothing between 11:29 and 11:48 PM.

evidence.name: Firmware push schedule
evidence.description: The outage matches a firmware push scheduled two weeks in advance.

evidence.name: Deleted temporary archive
evidence.description: A partially overwritten copy of the archive in the server's temp space.

evidence.name: Equipment register entry
evidence.description: USB device NX-8831 is signed out to Ethan Blake and never returned.

evidence.name: Empty coat pocket
evidence.description: Olivia's coat is in the cloakroom. The badge pocket is empty and the lining is pulled.

evidence.name: Live contractor account
evidence.description: Ethan Blake's account was flagged for revocation but remains partly active.

evidence.name: Badge and login mismatch
evidence.description: Ryan's credentials were used while Ryan's badge was outside the building.

evidence.name: Exit interview record
evidence.description: Ethan's exit interview was held on the third floor, beside the cloakroom.

timeline.text: A disabled contractor account attempts to authenticate.
Ryan receives an automated suspicious-login alert.
The server corridor camera stops recording.
A badge opens the side entrance.

hints: An account is not a person. Ask who could physically be at the keyboard.
Three people look guilty because their property was used. Find who had access to all three.
The cloakroom is on the same floor as the room used for exit interviews.
